pattern_name: Block-boundary input/output delay budgeting between unimplemented blocks
situation: Top-level integration where Block A launches to Block B and neither block is implemented yet, need to assign set_input_delay to B and set_output_delay from A to close top level early
derivation: Step1: Get top-level period T (e.g., T=1000ps confidence 1.0 if given). Step2: Estimate top-level interconnect between blocks: assumes 15% of T for 28nm (confidence 0.6) and 25% of T for 7nm-and-below (confidence 0.55) due to via resistance. So T_interconnect = T * 0.15 (confidence 0.6). Step3: Estimate uncertainty/jitter: assumes 10% of T (confidence 0.65) for setup. Step4: Remaining budget T_remain = T - T_interconnect - T_uncert = T * 0.75 (confidence 0.6). Step5: Split between launch and capture based on logic depth from RTL: if balanced, 50%/50% of T_remain (confidence 0.6); if one block is known control-heavy, 40%/60% (confidence 0.5). Step6: For Block B input: set_input_delay -max = T_launch + T_interconnect (e.g., 0.375*T + 0.15*T = 0.525*T). For Block B input -min for hold: assumes 10% of T (confidence 0.5) to ensure short path not over-optimistic. For Block A output: set_output_delay -max = T_capture + T_interconnect.
wrong_way: Assign 50% period to each block and 0% to interconnect, or assign set_input_delay = 0.5*T and set_output_delay = 0.5*T independently, double-counting period and leaving no room for top-level wire; downstream fails with uncloseable top-level paths after both blocks harden, requiring ECO re-budget
defense: Show RTL stage count estimate per block, historical wire delay from previous similar floorplan with similar bump pitch, and top-level floorplan distance estimate; keep budget spreadsheet with T_launch/T_interconnect/T_capture columns and review with both block owners; validate with zero-interconnect top-level trial route
signoff_risk: Too tight (over-budgeting interconnect/launch): block becomes bloated, inserts excess buffers, area/power spiral, may still pass signoff but fails PPA; Too loose (under-budgeting interconnect): block passes alone but top-level fails setup with real wires, requires late re-budget and full block re-implementation
node_era_note: At 28nm interconnect estimate 10-15% of period was safe; at 7nm-and-below need 20-30% plus via ladder and BEOL variation margin due to thin wires

pattern_name: False path vs multicycle path decision and defense
situation: Long timing path that looks like setup failure but is functionally not exercised every cycle, e.g., config register to datapath, mode mux, one-hot FSM branch, or debug path
derivation: Step1: Trace enable condition: does path go through a MUX select that is static for N cycles? Check RTL: if select comes from config reg that only writes on boot, N >= 10 cycles (confidence 0.7). Step2: Check temporal exclusivity: can launch and capture happen in same cycle per spec? Run formal reachability or check simulation that config write and datapath active are mutually exclusive. Step3: If mutually exclusive never in same cycle for functional operation, candidate for set_false_path. If mutually exclusive for K cycles but re-converges, candidate for set_multicycle_path K. Example: N=2 cycles for double-flop mode change (confidence 0.6), so set_multicycle_path -setup 2 -hold 1. Step4: Validate that all side-paths covered: ensure no other timing arc uses same net without the static condition. Step5: Require waiver: list startpoint-endpoint pair plus RTL condition signal name.
wrong_way: Mark any failing long path as false path to close timing quickly without proving static condition, or mark a true multicycle as false, or mark as multicycle 2 when hold needs explicit -hold 1 handling; silently breaks because synthesis/place no longer fixes path, but in rare functional mode path is active and silicon fails at speed or hold fails in silicon due to missing hold multicycle
defense: Provide waveform showing config stable for >N cycles, formal proof of mutual exclusivity, or static signal tied in this mode (case analysis); show CDC or mode constraint file that forces MUX select; get architect sign-off on mode table; keep false path list in version-controlled exceptions file with comment referencing spec section
signoff_risk: Too loose (false when should be multicycle or timed): path unbounded, late transition causes functional failure at speed, not caught at signoff STA because exception hides it; Too tight (timed when should be false): over-constrains implementation, creates congestion and setup/hold ping-pong, may still signoff but with PPA penalty and possible hold fixes that hurt setup
node_era_note: At 28nm false paths often tolerated; at 7nm-and-below false paths hide OCV and aging effects, reviewers require formal proof plus set_clock_groups handling

pattern_name: Clock-domain crossing max-delay budgeting for 2-flop sync and async FIFO
situation: Signal crossing from clkA to clkB asynchronous, protected by 2-flop synchronizer or async FIFO pointers, need SDC to prevent STA from timing it as synchronous
derivation: Step1: Identify sync chain: first flop after crossing is synchronizer, mark set_false_path or set_asynchronous_group between clocks, or set_max_delay -datapath_only. Step2: For data with valid handshake, constrain data delay to be less than destination period to ensure it is stable when sampled: assumes max allowed = 80% of min(dest period, source period) (confidence 0.6) minus 15% margin for jitter (confidence 0.55). Example: if dest period = 1000ps (confidence 1.0), set_max_delay = 800ps (confidence 0.6) -datapath_only from launch to first sync flop. Step3: For FIFO pointers gray-coded, set_max_delay = 1 * dest period (confidence 0.65) and set_min_delay = 0 for hold. Step4: Do NOT cut control path with same max: sync chain itself gets set_false_path -from launch -to sync0 to allow unlimited metastability resolution time, but keep set_max_delay on data bus.
wrong_way: Apply set_clock_groups -asynchronous to both data and control without max-delay, which allows data to have infinite delay and FIFO pointer to drift multiple cycles, causing functional CDC bug that STA hides; or apply set_false_path to data bus instead of control, silently allowing 10ns route on 1GHz interface
defense: Show synchronizer schematic, point to 2-flop chain in RTL, provide CDC tool report (e.g., Questa CDC) that data is qualified by synchronized valid, and show max-delay report that data arrives within one dest clock; retain pointer gray-coding proof
signoff_risk: Too loose (pure false path on data): CDC passes STA but fails in silicon due to data changing during sync window, metastability + data incoherence, signoff CDC checker will flag unbounded delay; Too tight (max-delay too small, e.g., 20% of period): implementation over-constrains, fails to route, forces unnecessary pipelining
node_era_note: At 28nm set_clock_groups -asynchronous often sufficient; at 7nm-and-below need set_max_delay -datapath_only plus OCV-aware margin due to larger variation on short cross-domain nets

situation: Early floorplan/placement stage where wire estimates are optimistic and late degradation from CTS, routing, and OCV is expected
derivation: Step1: Start with target period T. Step2: Apply over-constraint factor: assumes 15% over-constraint (confidence 0.6) at synthesis, so T_synth = T * 0.85 (confidence 0.6). Step3: Add clock uncertainty: assumes 10% of T for early stage (confidence 0.65) vs 5% at signoff (confidence 0.7). Step4: Keep input/output delays at nominal, do NOT over-constrain both period and IO simultaneously; only over-constrain core. Step5: Staged relaxation: after CTS, relax to 7% over-constraint (confidence 0.55) (T * 0.93), after route to 3% (confidence 0.5) (T * 0.97), before signoff to 0%. Step6: Track slack histogram: if worst slack >20% of T (confidence 0.6) early, indicates too much margin still available.
wrong_way: Over-constrain period by 30% (confidence misapplied) AND set_input_delay to 60% of period AND set_output_delay to 60% of period simultaneously, creating impossible 120% budget that forces tool to bloat logic and insert buffers everywhere, leading to power/area blowup and later unfixable congestion
defense: Show historical degradation curve from previous similar design: synthesis to place ~5% loss (confidence 0.55), place to CTS ~5% (confidence 0.55), CTS to route ~5-8% (confidence 0.5); justify over-constraint factor as sum of expected degradation; track QOR trend weekly and relax only when slack stable for 2 runs
signoff_risk: Too tight early: implementation becomes unnecessarily large, high power, congestion prevents closure, may still signoff but with 20-30% area penalty; Too loose early: early optimism hides real failures, late surprise with -200ps slack at route requiring full re-synthesis
node_era_note: At 28nm 10% over-constraint often enough; at 7nm-and-below need 15-20% due to via resistance and low-Vdd variation, but must relax earlier to avoid excessive low-Vt usage

situation: Chip-level IO interface where external device clock does not exist inside chip, need to model external launch/capture for set_input_delay and set_output_delay
derivation: Step1: create_clock -name VCLK -period T_ext equal to external device period (e.g., T_ext=1000ps confidence 1.0). Step2: Set virtual clock latency = 0 (confidence 1.0) because no internal network, but set uncertainty = board jitter + chip jitter: assumes 10% of T_ext (confidence 0.6). Step3: For input: set_input_delay -clock VCLK -max = T_board_max + T_ext_Tco_max + margin. Example: board delay max 300ps (confidence 0.6), Tco max 400ps (confidence 0.6), margin 50ps (confidence 0.5), so input max = 750ps. Set -min = board min + Tco min - margin (e.g., 100ps + 100ps -50ps =150ps). Step4: For output: set_output_delay -clock VCLK -max = T_board_max + T_setup_external (e.g., 300ps+200ps=500ps confidence 0.6), -min = T_board_min - T_hold_external.
wrong_way: Constrain IO using internal generated clock that includes internal insertion delay, causing double-counting of clock latency: input delay appears to have extra 500ps insertion, tool over-constrains data path and fails IO timing that is actually external-only; or using same clock for both input and output with zero virtual latency causing hold miscalculation
defense: Provide external device datasheet Tco/Tsu/Th numbers, board trace length to delay conversion (approx 6ps per mm (confidence 0.5)), and show virtual clock has no source latency; cross-check with IBIS or board simulation; keep VCLK separate per IO bank
signoff_risk: Too tight (large input/output delay): chip fails to close IO timing, adds unnecessary pipeline, may still signoff but with reduced Fmax; Too loose (small delay): chip passes internal STA but fails at system level on board, setup/hold failure at external device not caught until lab
node_era_note: At 28nm virtual clock latency 0 was sufficient; at 7nm-and-below need to model board and package via separate clock latency and include package trace variation

pattern_name: Generated and divided clock constraint derivation
situation: Internal clock divider, muxed clock, or PLL output that is not master clock, need correct timing relationship for STA
derivation: Step1: Master clock period T_master (e.g., 1000ps confidence 1.0). Step2: create_generated_clock -source [get_pin divider/Q] -divide_by N (e.g., N=2 confidence 1.0) so T_gen = T_master * N = 2000ps. Step3: If divided by 2 with 50% duty, set edges -edges {1 3 5} or -divide_by 2. Step4: Clock latency: generated clock latency = master insertion + divider cell delay: assumes divider delay 30ps (confidence 0.5) + wire 20ps (confidence 0.5). Step5: Uncertainty: master uncertainty 50ps (confidence 0.6) + divider jitter 20ps (confidence 0.5) = 70ps total (confidence 0.55). Step6: Set clock groups: if muxed clocks are mutually exclusive, set_clock_groups -physically_exclusive, else -logically_exclusive; do NOT use -asynchronous unless truly asynchronous.
wrong_way: Create generated clock with -combinational instead of -divide_by, losing edge relationship and causing STA to analyze 1-cycle path as 2-cycle or vice versa; or forget to set generated clock source latency, leading to 0 skew assumption and hold failures in silicon; or use set_clock_groups -asynchronous for muxed synchronous clocks, hiding synchronous transfer
defense: Show clock divider schematic, simulation showing divided edge aligns to master, and report_clocks showing master is source; verify with report_clock -skew that generated relationship matches RTL expectation; check that generated clock period matches measured division in gate sim
signoff_risk: Too tight (wrong divide factor, e.g., divide_by 4 instead of 2): half the paths appear as multicycle incorrectly, tool under-fixes, silicon fails at double frequency; Too loose (false -asynchronous between related generated clocks): cross-clock paths not timed, potential setup/hold failure between divide domains that are actually synchronous
node_era_note: At 28nm generated clock auto-derived often worked; at 7nm-and-below need explicit -master_clock and latency adjustment due to large divider variation and duty-cycle distortion

pattern_name: System-synchronous and source-synchronous output budgeting with board trace
situation: Chip drives data and clock/strobe to external device, need to split timing budget between chip, board, and external setup/hold
derivation: Step1: External device requires T_setup_ext = 200ps (confidence 0.6) and T_hold_ext = 100ps (confidence 0.6) at its pins. Step2: Board trace mismatch between clock and data: assumes max skew 50ps (confidence 0.55) due to 8mm mismatch (6ps/mm confidence 0.5). Step3: For source-synchronous (clock and data both from chip, edge-aligned): set_output_delay -max = T_board_max + T_setup_ext + board_skew_max = 300ps+200ps+50ps=550ps (confidence 0.6), set_output_delay -min = T_board_min - T_hold_ext - board_skew (e.g., 100ps-100ps-50ps = -50ps) meaning hold may be negative allowed. Step4: For system-synchronous (common board clock): output delay must include full period: set_output_delay -max = T_period - (T_setup_ext + board). Step5: Add margin 5% of period (confidence 0.6) for OCV.
wrong_way: Use same output delay for both source-sync and system-sync, ignoring that source-sync budget is board+setup only while system-sync includes period, causing either impossible timing (system-sync too tight) or under-constrained source-sync that fails on board due to unmodeled trace skew
defense: Provide board stackup and trace length report, external device datasheet with setup/hold numbers, and diagram showing clock-data alignment (center-aligned vs edge-aligned); show calculation spreadsheet with board min/max separate and justify margin from SI simulation
signoff_risk: Too tight: over-constrains output path, forces large drivers and hurts power, may still signoff but with SI issues; Too loose: chip passes STA but board fails because external setup/hold violated in corner, found only in lab with pattern-dependent failures
node_era_note: At 28nm board skew 50ps often negligible vs 2ns period; at 7nm-and-below with 1GHz+ source-sync, 50ps board skew is 5% of period and must be budgeted explicitly

pattern_name: Asynchronous handshake interface max/min delay constraint
situation: Asynchronous SRAM, flash, or custom handshake where request, address, data have no common clock, timing is relative between signals
derivation: Step1: Identify handshake: e.g., req launches, ack returns, data must be stable before ack. Step2: Do NOT use set_input_delay with period; use set_max_delay and set_min_delay between related signals. Step3: Example: req to data valid: set_max_delay -from [get_ports req] -to [get_ports data] = T_external_access_max + board_max = 10ns (confidence 0.6) (e.g., SRAM access 8ns (confidence 0.6) + board 2ns (confidence 0.5)). Step4: Hold: set_min_delay = board_min + hold requirement of external device = 1ns (confidence 0.5). Step5: For bidirectional, separate read and write constraints with -rise/-fall and case analysis on direction pin. Step6: False path all unrelated clocks to these IOs to avoid period-based analysis interfering.
wrong_way: Constrain async interface with create_clock + set_input_delay using arbitrary 10ns period, causing STA to check against non-existent clock edge and either miss true max-delay violation or create artificial multicycle; or apply set_false_path to entire async interface, allowing unbounded delay and silicon read failure
defense: Provide external device timing diagram showing req->data relationship without clock, and board trace delays; show that max-delay constraint directly models access time, not period; include protocol assertion that req de-asserts after ack, proven by formal
signoff_risk: Too tight (max-delay too small): implementation fails to meet impossible async timing, forces unnecessary pipelining and area; Too loose (false path): path can be 20ns but STA reports no violation, chip fails to read external memory at speed, caught only in system test
node_era_note: At 28nm async interfaces often handled with simple false path; at 7nm-and-below need explicit max/min delay plus SI-aware derating due to long board traces and on-die variation
